info.title: OpenPartner API
info.description:
The OpenPartner tenant API: partners, programs, links, attribution, commissions, payouts, reporting, webhooks and export. Use it to run a referral or affiliate program from your own backend, for example an in-app "Refer & earn" page with no separate OpenPartner login. Walkthrough: [Build an in-app referral page](https://github.com/getcoherence/openpartner/blob/main/docs/headless-referral.md). This document is generated from the API's own request validators. It is served at `/openapi.json`, and the rendered reference at `/docs`, on every deployment. White-label custom domains don't serve them; use the platform host, e.g. `https://app.openpartner.dev/api/docs`. ## Base URL and tenancy Every path below is relative to your tenant's API base: | Deployment | API base | Share links | | --- | --- | --- | | OpenPartner Cloud | `https://app.openpartner.dev/api/t/` | `https://app.openpartner.dev/r//` | | Cloud with a white-label domain | `https:///api` | `https:///r/` | | Self-hosted, single tenant | your API origin, e.g. `https://api.example.com` (or `/api` behind the bundled proxy) | `/r/` | | Self-hosted, multi-tenant | `/t/` (or `/api/t/`) | `/r//` | The slug comes **after** `/api`. `https://app.openpartner.dev/t//api/...` reaches the portal's static site, not the API, and returns HTML. On a multi-tenant deployment a request with no `/t/` prefix fails with `400 tenant_slug_missing`, and an unknown slug gets a plain `404`. Your slug is the `/t//` segment in your admin portal's address. Keys minted through the API are bound to their tenant. A key sent to another tenant's path is `401 unauthorized`. ## Authentication Send a key as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer op_…`. Keys are server-side credentials: never ship one to a browser or mobile app. There are three kinds: - **Admin key.** Unscoped, full access to the tenant. Minted with `POST /api-keys`, or the deployment's `ADMIN_API_KEY` (self-host). The admin portal's session cookie is accepted wherever an admin key is. - **Scoped key.** Minted with `POST /api-keys/scoped` and a list of scopes. It can call only the operations its scopes unlock, and it acts on any partner in the tenant. Calling something it lacks the scope for returns `403 forbidden_scope` with the `required` scope; calling an operation with no scope returns `403 forbidden`. Use one for every integration so a leaked key can't do everything. - **Partner key.** Minted with `POST /partners/{id}/api-keys` by an admin or the partner. It acts as that one partner and can only reach that partner's own resources (`/partners/{its id}/…`). Revoking the partner revokes its keys. Each operation says which of these it accepts. Scopes: | Scope | Unlocks | | --- | --- | | `clicks:write` | `POST /clicks` | | `commissions:read` | `GET /partners/{id}/commissions`
`GET /commissions` | | `events:write` | `POST /attribution/events`
`POST /attribution/conversions`
`POST /coupons/redeem` | | `links:read` | `GET /partners/{id}/links` | | `links:write` | `POST /partners/{id}/links` | | `partners:read` | `GET /partners`
`GET /partners/{id}`
`GET /partners/{id}/dashboard`
`GET /partners/{id}/timeseries`
`GET /partners/{id}/events`
`GET /partners/{id}/customers`
`GET /partners/{id}/breakdowns` | | `partners:write` | `POST /partners`
`POST /import/partners-csv`
`POST /partners/{id}/invite`
`POST /partners/{id}/revoke`
`POST /partners/{id}/coupons`
`DELETE /partners/{id}/coupons/{couponId}` | | `payouts:read` | `GET /partners/{id}/payouts` | | `webhooks:write` | `POST /webhooks`
`DELETE /webhooks/{id}` | `partners:read` also unlocks `GET /brand-resources` (brand logo, colours and shareable assets), which this reference doesn't cover yet. The OpenPartner Network federation key holds `partners:write`, `partners:read`, `links:write`, `commissions:read`, `clicks:write`. **Scoped reads that don't exist yet:** `GET /partners/{id}/funnel`, `/coupons` and `/commission-snapshot` accept no scope. Read them with an admin key from your server, or use `/timeseries` (which has `partners:read`) for funnel-like counts. ## Requests and responses - JSON bodies (`content-type: application/json`), up to 1 MB. `POST /import` takes up to 256 MB on single-tenant installs. - Errors are `{ "error": "", "detail": … }`. Branch on `error`; `detail` is for humans. - **Timestamps are ISO-8601 in UTC and must end in `Z`**: `2026-10-16T10:00:00Z`. An offset such as `+00:00` (Python's `isoformat()` default) is rejected with `400 invalid_body` / `invalid_query`. - Money in major units. Commission and payout amounts, and `eventValue` in webhook payloads, are decimal **strings** such as `"12.50"`. Report endpoints (dashboard, timeseries, a partner's events list) return JSON numbers. - Fields may be added to any response at any time. Ignore fields you don't know. - Send `X-Request-Id` to correlate a call; every response echoes one back (generated if you didn't send it). Quote it in support requests. ## Idempotency `POST /attribution/events` and `POST /coupons/redeem` take an `externalEventId`: your stable id for that one event. A retry with the same key replays the original result (`replayed: true`) and records nothing, even when the duplicates arrive at the same moment. A key reused for a different event is `409 external_event_id_conflict`. `POST /clicks` is idempotent on the click `id`. Other writes are not idempotent: `POST /partners` answers a duplicate email with `409 email_taken`, so look the partner up with `GET /partners?email=`. ## Pagination `GET /partners` and the commission lists are keyset-paginated: pass the response's `nextCursor` as `cursor` until it is `null`. Cursors are opaque. `GET /partners/{id}/events` and `/customers` use `limit` + `offset`. `GET /partners/{id}/payouts` returns the 200 most recent, and `GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries` the 100 most recent. ## Rate limits The API shares one limit of **600 requests per 5 minutes per client IP** across its routes (a few infrastructure paths are exempt). A backend calls from one IP, so that is your whole integration's budget, event ingest included: at four calls per page view, about 150 uncached page views per 5 minutes. Cache partner stats for a few minutes, don't let users force a refresh, and report events from a queue that backs off on `429`. Over the limit you get `429 rate_limited` with the IETF `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers. `POST /attribution/identify` has its own limit of 120 per minute per IP, answered with `429 rate_limited` and `Retry-After`. When the browser SDK calls it, that is each visitor's IP; when your backend calls it, every stitch counts against your backend's IP, so prefer the browser for identify at volume. ## Webhooks Subscribe with `POST /webhooks`; the event catalogue is under **Webhook events**. Each delivery is a JSON `POST` of an envelope `{ id, event, created, data }` with: | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `X-OpenPartner-Signature` | hex HMAC-SHA256 of `.`, keyed with the endpoint's secret (the whole `whsec_…` string) | | `X-OpenPartner-Timestamp` | Unix seconds when the attempt was signed | | `X-OpenPartner-Event` | the event type | | `X-OpenPartner-Delivery` | the envelope `id` | To verify a delivery, recompute the HMAC over the **raw** request body, before any JSON parsing, and compare it in constant time. Reject timestamps more than 5 minutes from now. Then dedupe on `id`: ```js import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto'; function verify(rawBody, headers, secret) { const ts = headers['x-openpartner-timestamp']; const sig = headers['x-openpartner-signature'] ?? ''; if (!ts || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(ts)) > 300) return false; const expected = Buffer.from(createHmac('sha256', secret).update(`${ts}.${rawBody}`).digest('hex')); const given = Buffer.from(sig); return given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(given, expected); } ``` Delivery is at most once per trigger: a non-2xx answer, a redirect, or no answer within 10 seconds marks the delivery failed, and **failed deliveries are not retried automatically**. Find them with `GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries` and resend with `POST /webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{deliveryId}/retry`. A resend carries the same `id` and a fresh signature. Treat webhooks as notifications and the list endpoints as the record: reconcile from `GET /commissions` if you can't afford to miss one. Endpoints must be publicly reachable. Private, loopback and link-local destinations are refused at delivery time, and OpenPartner Cloud delivers only to ports 80 and 443. A single-tenant self-host can allow specific private ranges with `OPENPARTNER_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS`.

adminKey.description: An unscoped admin key (`POST /api-keys`), or the deployment's `ADMIN_API_KEY`. Full access to the tenant it was minted in. Server-side only.

scopedKey.description: A scoped key (`POST /api-keys/scoped`). Each operation lists the one scope that unlocks it; a key without it gets `403 forbidden_scope`. Operations that list no scope reject scoped keys.

partnerKey.description: A partner-scoped key (`POST /partners/{id}/api-keys`). Acts as that one partner: it can read and write only that partner's own resources.

postbackToken.name: token
postbackToken.description: The conversion postback token (`opcp_…`), minted and rotated under Admin → Integrations. It travels in the URL, so proxies, browser history and the sender's own logs keep it. It is built to be cheap to leak: it records conversions and nothing else, is never accepted as a Bearer key, can be pinned to the sender's IPs, and rotating it kills the old URL at once. Only `GET /postback` takes it.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON you supplied at creation. OpenPartner may add a `network` key when the partner is synced to the Network.

activatedAt.description: Null until the partner accepts their invite. `sendInvite: false` sets it at creation.

detail.description: Human-readable cause, or zod `flatten()` output for `invalid_body` / `invalid_query`.

Error.description: Every non-2xx response. `error` is stable and safe to branch on; `detail` is for humans and may change. Some errors carry extra fields (e.g. `required` on `forbidden_scope`, `matureAt` on `holdback_active`).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

Decimal.description: A decimal amount as a string, e.g. `"12.50"`. Major currency units.

CommissionBands.description: Value bands: the rate steps up with the event's value. The sub-rule's own `value` is the base band; `levels` lists the steps above it. `whole` pays the reached band's rate on the whole value, `marginal` pays each slice at its own band's rate.

CommissionTiers.description: Performance tiers: the rate steps up with the partner's own revenue or conversions over a window. Not combined with `bands`.

programId.description: Null for partner-wide terms; set for terms on that one program.

CommissionSnapshot.description: A per-partner commission override. When present it replaces the program's rule for this partner's future commissions: on every program (partner-wide, `programId` null) or on one program. On that program, program-scoped terms beat partner-wide ones.

CommissionRule.description: An array of triggered sub-rules. Programs written through this API always store the array; rows created before compound rules may still hold the legacy single-rule object.

holdbackDays.description: Above 0: commissions auto-approve this many days after accruing. 0 or null: they wait for a manual approve.

customerRewardDelivery.description: How customer-side rewards reach the customer on this deployment: minted in Stripe, not configured, or applied by the brand itself.

source.description: Partner callers only: how the grant was made.

commission.description: This partner's terms on this program (setPartnerProgramCommission). Null: the partner-wide override, or the program's own rule, applies.

destinationUrl.description: Deep-link override. Null = the program's destinationUrl.

Link.description: A partner share link. The public URL is built from the router base, not stored: `https://app.openpartner.dev/r/<tenantSlug>/<linkKey>` on OpenPartner Cloud, `https://<custom-domain>/r/<linkKey>` on a white-label domain, `<router-origin>/r/<linkKey>` self-hosted.

firstStitch.description: False when this (cref, userId) pair was already stitched; nothing was written.

backfilledAttributions.description: Events already recorded for this userId that attributed now that the click is known.

status.description: `not_attributed` appears only on a replay of an event that did not attribute the first time; which miss it was is not stored.

replayed.description: Present when an earlier call with the same `externalEventId` already recorded this event. `eventId` and `attribution` are that call's.

externalEventId.description: Idempotency key: your stable id for this one event, up to 120 characters. A number is used as its string. `null`, `""` or a blank string mean no key.

userId.description: The user the click was stitched to: your `userId`, or the click's own synthetic user when you sent none.

replayed.description: Present when an earlier call with the same `externalEventId` already recorded this conversion. `eventId` and `attribution` are that call's.

externalEventId.description: Idempotency key: your stable id for this one conversion (a loan or transaction id), up to 120 characters. A number is used as its string.

canEdit.description: The program lets partners rename their own codes.
The program lets partners rename their own codes.

status.description: `paid` means the commission is in a payout. On the manual rail that happens when the payout is planned, before the money is sent: check the payout's own `status`.

metadata.description: How the amount was worked out, where it took more than the rule's flat value. A banded or tiered rule records `slab`: which sub-rule (`ruleIndex`), `kind` (`band` or `tier`), the `level` reached and its `threshold` and `value`, and for tiers the `metric` and its `metricValue` over the `window`. Empty for a flat rule.

campaignName.description: The program's name (kept under its pre-rename key).

matureAt.description: When the holdback ends and the commission becomes approvable. Null = no holdback.

status.description: `paid` means the commission is in a payout. On the manual rail that happens when the payout is planned, before the money is sent: check the payout's own `status`.

metadata.description: How the amount was worked out, where it took more than the rule's flat value. A banded or tiered rule records `slab`: which sub-rule (`ruleIndex`), `kind` (`band` or `tier`), the `level` reached and its `threshold` and `value`, and for tiers the `metric` and its `metricValue` over the `window`. Empty for a flat rule.

status.description: A `manual` payout stays `pending` until you send the money and confirm it; only `paid` means it went out.

commissionByStatus.description: Sum of commission amounts accrued since `since`, keyed by status, across all currencies (no conversion). Statuses with nothing are absent. `paid` includes manual payouts not yet sent: read payouts for money that went out.

sampleSize.description: User-agent dimensions only: clicks sampled (newest first).

identities.description: Distinct users stitched to those clicks.

signups.description: Distinct users with an attributed `signup` event.

paid.description: Distinct users with an attributed `invoice_paid` event.

secretPrefix.description: First characters of the signing secret, to tell secrets apart. The secret itself is only returned at creation.

payload.description: The exact envelope that was sent.

plaintext.description: The key. Shown once and never stored; keep it server-side.

ExportBundle.description: The whole tenant, re-importable by a self-hosted instance (`POST /import`).

credentials.description: Fresh credentials for restored rows, per table, shown once. `WebhookEndpoint`: `{ id, url, secret }` for each endpoint restored (paused until you turn it back on).

autoEnroll.description: Stored name for "offer the Network to my partners". When `enabled && autoEnroll`, partners are asked whether to join, and only those who opt in are shared (name and email; never `metadata`).

post.description:
Creates a partner and grants it programs.

- `sendInvite: false` creates the partner **active immediately** and sends no email. Use this when your own app is the partner's UI (headless / in-app referral). The default sends a magic-link invite.
- `programIds` omitted grants **every current program**. Pass an explicit list (even `[]`) to control access.
- A coupon is auto-minted per granted program.
- Fires `partner.created`.

**Email and portal access.** A `sendInvite: false` partner is active, so anyone who knows its email can request a sign-in link on the hosted partner portal (`POST /auth/signin`): OpenPartner then emails that address, and the partner can use the portal. There is no setting to turn that off per partner yet. If that matters, give headless partners an address that can't receive mail.

**OpenPartner Network:** this call shares nothing with the OpenPartner Network. A partner's name and email reach it only if the partner opts in themselves, while the tenant offers the Network (`autoEnroll` on, `GET /config/network`): they're asked on the join page, once on first portal sign-in, and in a portal setting. `metadata` is never sent. To keep customer-referral partners from being asked, turn offering off: `POST /config/network {"autoEnroll": false}`.

On OpenPartner Cloud the brand needs an active plan (`402 plan_required`) and an approved account (`403 brand_pending_review`).

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `partners:write`.

get.description:
Newest first, keyset-paginated. `email` is an exact match ("find by email"); `q` is a case-insensitive substring match on name or email. Filters keep the same order and cursor scheme.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `partners:read`.
**Access:** admin key, a scoped key with `partners:read`, or the partner's own key (`:id` must be that partner).

post.description:
Creates many partners in one request: the way to load an existing customer base without spending your rate limit on one `POST /partners` per row.

Send `text/csv` with a header row: `email` and `name` (required), `activatedAt` (ISO-8601, default now) and `metadata` (a JSON object string, e.g. `"{""appUserId"":""u_1""}"`). Quoted fields may contain commas but not line breaks. Tools that can't send `text/csv` can POST `{"csv": "..."}` as JSON instead.

Unlike `POST /partners`, an import:
- grants every partner **every current program** (there is no `programIds`),
- sends no email, mints no coupons, fires no `partner.created` webhooks,
- shares nothing with the OpenPartner Network: as with `POST /partners`, only a partner's own opt-in does.

Rows whose email already exists are reported as `skipped_email_taken` with the existing `partnerId`, so re-running an import is safe. `?dryRun=true` validates and reports without writing. The file is written in one transaction, so a failed import writes nothing. A repeated email later in the same file is skipped like one already on the roster. Send very large rosters in batches of a few thousand rows.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `partners:write`.

schema.description: Validate and report without writing. Not validated by the route: only `true` and `1` switch it on.

row.description: Line number in the file, counting the header as 1.

For a partner who has not activated yet. For an applicant held for review, this is also the approval.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `partners:write`.

Ends the partner's sessions and partner keys and stops future attribution to them. Existing links keep redirecting (clicks are flagged `revoked`); past commissions are untouched.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `partners:write`.
**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

put.description:
Replaces the program's commission rule for this partner's future commissions on every program that has no program-scoped terms for them (see `setPartnerProgramCommission`). Omitting `commissionRules` clears any compound rules.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

Clears the partner-wide terms only. Program-scoped terms stay.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

get.summary: Get a partner's commission terms on one program
get.description: **Access:** admin key, or the partner's own key (`:id` must be that partner). Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

put.summary: Set a partner's commission terms on one program
put.description:
Same body as `setPartnerCommissionOverride`, for one program. On that program these terms beat the partner-wide override and set the holdback too (omitted = the program's own). The partner doesn't need a grant on the program: terms can be agreed before access, and outlive a revoked grant.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

delete.summary: Clear a partner's commission terms on one program
delete.description:
Commissions on the program fall back to the partner-wide override, or the program's rule.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

get.description: **Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

post.description:
A program is one set of terms: commission rule, attribution window and model, destination URL.

`shareOnNetwork` defaults to **true** when the tenant is on the OpenPartner Network, which lists the program on the public marketplace and makes `marketplaceDescription` required. Pass `shareOnNetwork: false` for a private program such as customer referral.

`holdbackDays` above 0 means commissions are **approved automatically** that many days after they accrue (by the scheduled jobs), and then paid by the next payout run. 0 or omitted means every commission waits for `POST /commissions/{id}/approve`.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

get.summary: Programs the caller can create links for
get.description:
A partner sees its granted programs that are currently active. An admin sees every program. Commission terms aren't included.

**Access:** admin key or a partner key. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

patch.description:
Changes apply to future commissions. Partners with a commission override keep it.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

get.summary: List programs with this partner's grant state
get.description: **Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

200.description: Every program, flagged granted or not.

Idempotent. Unknown program ids are skipped. Mints a coupon per newly granted program.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

Blocks new links on that program and retires the partner's coupons on it. Existing links keep redirecting.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

get.description: **Access:** admin key, a scoped key with `links:read`, or the partner's own key (`:id` must be that partner).

post.description:
`linkKey` is the short code in the share URL and is unique per tenant. A partner caller must hold a grant for the program; admin and scoped callers don't. `destinationUrl` overrides the program's destination only when the program allows deep links to that host.

**Access:** admin key, a scoped key with `links:write`, or the partner's own key (`:id` must be that partner).

post.summary: Stitch a click to a user
post.description:
Links the click id (`cref`) a visitor arrived with to your user id. The browser SDK calls this on signup and login; your backend can call it instead if it receives the `cref`.

Repeat calls for the same pair are no-ops. Events already recorded for the user are attributed when the stitch lands (`backfilledAttributions`). Calling it on login too stitches a user who clicked on another device; until a pending fix ships, a second click stitched to a user with already-attributed events can credit those events again, so prefer calling it at signup.

Unauthenticated by design. It accepts any origin (CORS) and is limited to 120 requests per minute per client IP. Use the same `userId` you later send to `POST /attribution/events`.

**Access:** public, no API key. Rate-limited per client IP.

Server-to-server conversion ingest. The event is attributed to the partner whose click the user was stitched to (within the program's window and model) and commissions accrue.

**Event types.** Any string is accepted. Two have built-in meaning:
- `signup` is the funnel's *signups* stage (`signup` and `trial_started` are *leads* in the timeseries).
- `invoice_paid` is the funnel's *paid* stage, and on OpenPartner Cloud it is billable GMV, as is `subscription_created`. Report payments as `invoice_paid`. Other types with a value still accrue commission but are not counted as GMV.

`value` is in major units (`49.99`), defaulting to no value; `currency` defaults to USD.

**Idempotency.** Always send `externalEventId`: your system's stable id for this one event (invoice id, order id, deal id + stage). A retry with the same key returns `200` with `replayed: true` and the original result, writing nothing. Reusing a key for a different userId, type, value or currency returns `409 external_event_id_conflict`. Keys are per tenant, up to 120 characters, and shared with `POST /coupons/redeem`.

**Don't report a payment twice.** If your Stripe account also sends webhooks to this deployment (`/webhooks/stripe`, self-host), those payments are already recorded, keyed by the Stripe event id. Reporting the same payment here under your own invoice id records it a second time.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `events:write`.

post.summary: Record a conversion against a click
post.description:
For senders that hold a click id but never saw an identify: a lender reporting a funded loan, a CRM, an affiliate network. The click id reaches them through the destination URL's `{click_id}` macro, or the `cref` the router appends. One call stitches the click to a user and records the event, in one transaction.

Send `userId` when you have your own id for the user: attribution then follows the program's model across every click that user is stitched to, as on `POST /attribution/events`. Without it the click's own synthetic user is used, and this click alone is credited. Events recorded for the user before this stitch are not backfilled; `POST /attribution/identify` does that.

**Idempotency.** `externalEventId` is required. A retry with the same key returns `200` with `replayed: true` and the original result, even if the click has been flagged since. Reusing a key for a different click, userId, type, value or currency returns `409 external_event_id_conflict`. Keys share one namespace with `POST /attribution/events`, `GET /postback` and `POST /coupons/redeem`.

A click flagged by velocity limits or a revoked partner earns nothing: `422 click_flagged`.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `events:write`.

get.summary: Record a conversion from a postback URL
get.description:
`POST /attribution/conversions` for senders that can only fire a URL: affiliate networks, many lenders, tracking pixels. Same result: the click is stitched to a user and the event recorded, in one transaction.

```
GET /postback?click_id={click_id}&type=sale&amount=49.00&currency=USD&txn_id={transaction_id}&token=opcp_…
```

**The token is in the URL.** Proxies, browser history and the sender's own logs keep query strings, so treat a postback URL as leaked from the day you hand it out, and use `POST /attribution/conversions` with a Bearer key whenever the sender can set a header. The postback token is built for this: it records conversions and nothing else, is never accepted as a Bearer key (and an API key is never accepted as `token`), can be pinned to the sender's IPs (`ipAllowlist`), and rotating it on the Integrations page stops the old URL at once. OpenPartner's own request log redacts it. Always use `https://`.

**Idempotency.** `txn_id` is the `externalEventId`: a network re-firing the postback records once. Keys share one namespace with `POST /attribution/conversions`, `POST /attribution/events` and `POST /coupons/redeem`, and reusing one for a different conversion is `409 external_event_id_conflict`.

**Responses are plain text**, not JSON: `ok`, or the error code (`invalid_parameters` is followed by the offending names, e.g. `invalid_parameters: click_id, txn_id`). Every response is `Cache-Control: no-store`. `HEAD` answers `405` and records nothing, so a link checker can't create a conversion.

The token is checked before anything else, so a caller without one learns nothing about the parameters or clicks. Mint it under **Admin → Integrations** (or `POST /conversion-postback/token`).

**Access:** the conversion postback token in the `token` query parameter. API keys are not accepted, as a Bearer header or as `token`.
